subject.title: refactor(macos): move PortGuardian state to SQLite

question: Should macOS PortGuardian adopt the signed, one-way SQLite storage cutover that blocks old JSON-writing copies from sharing the migrated state directory?
rationale: This is an intentional storage and code-signing boundary with downgrade and recovery consequences that tests alone cannot choose on behalf of maintainers.

options.title: Accept after final-head proof
options.body: Approve the one-way cutover after the prerequisite lands and redacted evidence demonstrates migration, old-copy exclusion, and orphan recovery on the reviewed head.

options.title: Require a different upgrade contract
options.body: Pause this stack and define an alternative supported downgrade or mixed-version policy before accepting the durable-state migration.

recommendation.title: Accept after final-head proof
recommendation.body: Approve the one-way cutover after the prerequisite lands and redacted evidence demonstrates migration, old-copy exclusion, and orphan recovery on the reviewed head.

likelyOwner.reason: The current stack author documented the storage and signed-copy design choices and is best positioned to route the requested decision to the appropriate repository owner.
